matches.rationale: Finding 1 directly notes the abstract misstates the bound as d^{O(1/ε)} instead of d^{O(1/ε²)}. Finding 7 also points out the abstract misstates the bound while claiming improvement. Both capture the same discrepancy in the abstract's calibration bound.

Finding 2 identifies that the abstract claims an exp(Ω(1/ε)) lower bound but Theorem 4.3 gives exp(Ω(ε^{-1/6})), overstating the exponential dependence. This matches the distortion of the necessity and tightness claim in the abstract.
No finding mentions the fabricated reference [ZKL23] or the specific claim that no known algorithm achieved sub-exponential dependence on d before 2025.
No finding addresses the reversal of arguments in the Bregman divergence definition or its consequences for Lemma 2.1.
No finding mentions the claim that TreeCal does not require knowledge of regularizers or ρ, nor the hidden dependence on ρ in parameter choices.
No finding discusses the confusing statement that TreeCal is nearly identical to [Pen25] while claiming analytical novelty.
No finding addresses the claim that the ℓ₂ calibration bound is independent of d while ignoring dimension dependence in diam(P).
No finding mentions the strong convexity definition or an incorrect inequality direction in Section 2.4.
No finding mentions the exaggerated claim that the algorithm 'completely solves the high-dimensional calibration problem'.
No finding mentions the change of constant from 3 to 1 in the swap regret bound of Theorem C.1.
No finding mentions missing funding disclosures or conflicts of interest related to Google Research affiliations.
No finding addresses the logical inconsistency between saying BTL is unimplementable and then discussing its regret in a practical context.
No finding discusses the misattribution of TreeSwap to prior work while framing the analysis as novel.
Finding 4 states that Claim C.3 asserts an inequality with ≥ while the proof derives ≤, exactly capturing the corrupted inequality direction and the resulting logical inconsistency.
No finding mentions the requirement of central symmetry and the overstatement that the results hold for arbitrary convex sets and norms.
No finding discusses the omission of computational cost analysis or the claim that TreeCal is 'highly efficient'.
No finding mentions the corruption of normalizing by T in the definition of calibration error in Section 2.1.
Finding 5 points out that the formal Theorem 4.3 states an exponent with d^{1/7} while the informal uses d^{1/14}, matching the corruption that changed the lower bound exponent from 1/14 to 1/7.
